newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition closer to pact on tax-newspaper.
newsitem.headline: German coalition closer to pact on tax-newspaper.

text.p: The partners in Germany's centre right coalition have come closer to an agreement in their dispute over how to plug the country's multi-billion-mark deficit hole, the Bild newspaper said on Tuesday.

The mass circulation daily said the Christian Democrats (CDU) and sister party Christian Socialist Union (CSU) had agreed in principle with junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) not to raise taxes to close the budget gap.
To compensate, various elements of taxation reform plans would be pushed through, with tax breaks in particular for large corporations to be drastically reduced, the Bild said.
"The Bonn coalition is fighting for its future," Bild said, without naming any sources.

FDP chairman Wolfgang Gerhardt had told journalists in Bonn on Monday the differences were narrowing between his party and Chancellor Helmut Kohl's CDU on new budget savings measures without tax increases in 1997 and 1998.
"The coalition will stick together," said Gerhardt.
Serious disagreements over the gaping holes for both the 1997 and 1998 budgets have torn at the threads of the coalition for months.
The FDP has firmly opposed any tax increases while Finance Minister Theo Waigel has refused to rule out raising some taxes in 1998.
